lessons.goal: 區分總價與單位價格，將需求納入購買。

questions.evidence: At a stationery shop, Mei compares two refill packs for her pen. A small pack contains four refills and costs sixty dollars. A large pack contains ten and costs one hundred and thirty. Both contain the same type of refill, and each refill fits her pen.
questions.prompt: How many refills are in the small pack?

questions.evidence: The large pack has a lower price per refill, but Mei needs only three before the school year ends. She will change to a different pen next year, so extra refills may not be useful. Her budget for today's purchase is one hundred dollars.

At a stationery shop, Mei compares two refill packs for her pen. A small pack contains four refills and costs sixty dollars. A large pack contains ten and costs one hundred and thirty. Both contain the same type of refill, and each refill fits her pen.

The large pack has a lower price per refill, but Mei needs only three before the school year ends. She will change to a different pen next year, so extra refills may not be useful. Her budget for today's purchase is one hundred dollars.

A friend offers to share the large pack and take six refills while Mei keeps four. They agree to divide its price according to the number each receives. The shop will sell the sealed pack to them together; they can separate the refills after paying.

Mei calculates her share before agreeing. Buying more is not automatically a saving, but a planned split can change the comparison. She checks that her friend really wants the same refill type and writes their agreement down.
